problem: "It is the best error-free data rate the channel can support" is too strong. Capacity is the highest rate at which the error probability can be made arbitrarily small (in the limit of long blocks). A student may read "error-free" as "a simple link can reach C with zero errors", which later material on the coding theorem contradicts.
fix: Channel capacity is the highest rate at which the channel can carry data with arbitrarily small error probability; no code can do better.

problem: The maximisation max over p(x) of I(X;Y) is stated without the average input power constraint. For a continuous channel with no power limit the mutual information can be made as large as we like, so the step to C = B log₂(1 + S/N) is unexplained and a student cannot see where S enters the maximisation.
fix: Add: the maximisation is over input distributions whose average power is at most S W (a Gaussian input then achieves it); only then does the maximum equal B log₂(1 + S/N).

problem: "at low SNR the absolute changes are smaller" is vague. Smaller than what, and in which units? A student may read it as "capacity barely changes at low SNR", which the plot (0.14 to 1 bit/s/Hz between −10 dB and 0 dB) can appear to contradict depending on how it is read.
fix: At high SNR each extra 3 dB adds about 1 bit/s/Hz; near 0 dB and below, each extra decibel adds well under 0.2 bit/s/Hz, so the curve flattens towards zero at low SNR.
